title: JsonUI API Mock Definition
description: Editor/documentation schema for *.mock.json. The CLI validates via validation/mock.py, not this file.

violationPaths.description: Paths the checker reports, e.g. '.crate.variants[].spec_digest'. A bare string is one path.

method.description: HTTP method. The tools uppercase before matching, so any case is accepted and the lowercase spellings are listed here for that reason -- an editor that marked `get` invalid would be rejecting input the CLI and the mock server both take. Uppercase is canonical and is what `mock generate` writes.

contractViolations.description: Contract violations this scenario makes ON PURPOSE — a mock that omits a required field is how a test proves the client fails closed when the server omits it. The contract check subtracts exactly the paths named here; an undeclared violation in the same scenario still fails, and a declaration that stops matching is reported (a negative scenario that quietly turned positive). Paths use the checker's spelling; '[]' matches every element of an array, '[0]' one.

skipRequestValidation.description: Do not check what the APP SENT against the swagger for this scenario. The mock server validates request bodies and query strings and RECORDS the violations (it never rejects — a 422 here would turn 'the implementation is wrong' into 'this screen should show an error' in every test that touches it). Set this on a scenario that deliberately drives a request the contract does not allow, so the recording stays a list of real problems.

undeclaredStatus.description: This scenario answers a status its operation does not declare, ON PURPOSE — a fail-open regression, or an edge the contract will never state. Without this the check gates on it (forms A and C: a code the contract declares somewhere, attached to an operation that does not declare it), and a gate a project cannot clear is one people learn to read past. Authoring-time only: nothing at runtime reads this key, so it carries no driver requirement.
